argument: The chapter's condition table ends Grappled and Restrained with an 'Escape action', and nothing in the book defines that action, so the chapter's own source-of-record section for grappling leaves the escapee's procedure unwritten. Grappling defines the initiation roll and then only what the holding character may spend an Action on (Pin, Throw, Choke); the held creature gets no cost, no roll, and no opposing side for breaking free. At the table this is a dead end the DA must improvise for a basic maneuver, and it is exactly where the section's pull-quote promise of continued counterplay fails: the escape procedure that promise implies was never written. The same table shows the chapter knows how to route an 'Ends' cell through a defined action, since Prone exits on Stand Up, which is printed in the Basic Maneuvers table and in the glossary; no Escape action appears in either. Tested and clean, for the record: the 56 achievable sorted D666 results are all mapped by the wound table and no named triple falls inside a listed range, and the worked example's HP, DR and morale arithmetic all recompute correctly. Tested and doubtful: the Surprise penalty and the Defend bonus are stated numerically in one table and as a Boon/Bane elsewhere, which is a separate conversion question I am not filing here.

evidence.claim: The Grappled row lists Escape action as the condition's only end condition.
The Restrained row ends the same way, again naming an action no chapter defines.
The Grappling section spells out only what the character doing the holding may spend an Action on, so it never states how the held creature gets out.
